chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Dave Duncan fits in; Grant Williams joins; the Louvre Ballroom
summary: Duncan wins the band over, guitarist Grant Williams joins, and Fields explains the all-white Louvre Ballroom where Fletcher Henderson played a week.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: (Side A of Tape 2 begins at this point.)
They kidded about Dave, but Dave--

Dave Duncan, okay boy, white, but he really had us in good condition and everybody got so that they liked him. Bruce Steele then came into the Tulsa club and the waiters and everybody started to talk about my group, and then one Grant Williams--I don't know if you heard, he played something on the style of Floyd Smith, guitar, and just like a lot of the guys, you know, how hard it was on the road, well I was just kind of stationary there, there wasn't much money, but they said they'd rather have a little money and know they are going to make it, than be out there and don't know what they're going to make. So Grant Williams joined the band, and he had been known-- now don't get confused about Fats Waller, but he was a saxophone player, I think he was
originally out of Detroit, known as Fats Walls.

He was a very fine sax man and this Grant Williams was with him, and of course he got very well known by him being with this band here, and they had played this Louvre Ballroom. If you had ever played in there, that was really the best. Fletcher Henderson did a week at the Louvre.
